findings.title: getClientsWithPermission cannot return real client IDs and adds a bogus 'Clients' entry
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission(String scope) collects results via resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). Per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (AdminPermissionsSchema.java line 104) with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) and never have their type set to "Clients", so findByType will not match them; the only resource that carries the type is the all-type resource itself, whose name is the literal string "Clients" — not a valid client ID. Consequently the method can only ever return an empty set, or a set containing the invalid entry "Clients" when an all-clients permission grants the requested scope. Any consumer that uses this set to filter client lists (the V1 contract returns client IDs for this purpose) will either silently drop all clients that have explicit per-client permissions, or attempt to resolve the non-existent client "Clients". There is no test covering this method, so the defect is not caught by the new tests.

findings.title: UnsupportedOperationException from inherited methods surfaces as HTTP 500 on existing admin REST endpoints
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from isPermissionsEnabled (line 188), setPermissionsEnabled (line 193), resource (line 198), getPermissions (line 203) and canExchangeTo (line 148). These methods are part of the inherited ClientPermissions contract and are still called by non-feature-gated code when the V2 feature is enabled: the standard admin endpoints GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions (ClientManagementPermissionsResource) call AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions. Since AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 feature flag is on (AdminPermissions.java line 67), those endpoints will return an uncontrolled HTTP 500 instead of a graceful 400/404 or a "not supported" response. The V2 feature should either gate these endpoints or return a proper error response rather than an unhandled runtime exception.

findings.title: No migration for existing admin-permissions realms: new Clients scopes and resource are never created
findings.body: init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists (lines 226-228). For realms where the admin permissions client was initialized by a previous build (i.e., before the Clients resource type was added to the schema), the new scopes "configure", "map-roles-client-scope" and "map-roles-composite" and the "Clients" all-type resource are never created, and no migration is included in this change. On such upgraded realms, creating any Clients permission fails: getScope() throws ModelValidationException("Scope [configure] does not exist.") and getOrCreateResource() throws ModelException("No scopes found.") (line 108) because the scopes cannot be resolved. Existing V2-enabled realms therefore break after upgrade until the admin permissions client is deleted and re-created.

findings.title: getResourceName not updated for the Clients resource type, returns null for client resources
findings.body: getResourceName() only special-cases the Users resource type (resolving "Users" to "All users" and per-user resources to the username). For the newly added Clients type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Per-client resources are created in getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) with name set to the client's internal ID and no display name, so getDisplayName() is null; the all-type "Clients" resource likewise has no display name. Any consumer of getResourceName (used to render resource names for permissions in the admin REST/console) will get null for every Clients permission, showing blank identifiers instead of the client name or an "All clients" label, unlike the Users behavior implemented in the same method.

findings.title: Null resource passed to findByResource in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when the per-client resource is not found the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) (line 217), which can return null (it returns null whenever supportsAuthorizationSchema is false, e.g. the realm's admin permissions are disabled while the admin permissions client and its resource server still exist). The result is passed directly to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) at line 219 without a null check — unlike the sibling hasPermission(String scope) at line 245 which does check for null. Depending on the store implementation this either relies on undefined behavior for a null lookup or risks a NullPointerException; the fallback should null-check the resource and return false, as the other overload does.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() claims they return a boolean
findings.body: The javadoc added in this PR for requireView() (line 96, "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.") and requireViewClientScopes() (line 101, "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.") describes a boolean return, but these are void methods that throw ForbiddenException when the check fails. The documentation should state that they throw ForbiddenException (as done for requireManage/requireConfigure/requireList), otherwise callers reading the interface may assume a return value.

findings.title: Dead code: unused getEvaluationContext, TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, Scope import and logger
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2 contains leftovers from an abandoned token-exchange implementation: the private method getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) (lines 262-272) is never called, the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) and the import of org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope (line 27) are unused, and the Logger field (line 51) is never used. This dead code should be removed together with the now-unsupported canExchangeTo, or the token-exchange support should be completed, so readers do not assume exchange evaluation is wired up.
